Hi Grace / Redwood account team,

We hit a significant issue this morning starting at ~07:50 UTC where realtime streaming responses to our user sessions intermittently go silent for 8-30s and then resume with a burst of tokens. We also observed elevated HTTP 5xx errors on the ingest route and several websocket connections dropping with close code 1006. Throughput for our primary tenant slipped ~45% at peak.

Observables:
- Trace id: 78b6c3a2-ff12-4a2b-9c4e
- Sample connection ids: conn-9822, conn-9829
- Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/streaming/brightleaf?panelId=streams (spike at 07:50)
- Attached: logs_20270719.tar.gz (server and client traces), sample_payload.txt

This is customer-impacting (user-visible gaps). Can you advise immediate mitigation and whether this is related to the keepalive/kv cache path? If we need to flip to a non-streaming fallback or route to dedicated capacity, we need the guidance now.

Thanks,

Thanks Sam & Grace — I’m looking at the traces now. A few quick thoughts from first-pass diagnostics:

1) The websocket close codes and server logs point to intermittent event-loop stalls on a subset of GPU workers that manifest as delayed chunk flushes. The gaps you see (8–30s) line up with worker side backpressure + batching pauses.
2) There are multiple clients hitting the same cache shard for prefix KV which can amplify stalls if that shard temporarily blocks.
3) We also see a lightweight surge in average sequence length for a subset of sessions (~+15 tokens) but that alone shouldn’t explain 45% throughput drop.

Short mitigations to try right away (with your OK):
- Enable our fallback routing to an alternate capacity pool in us-east-2 (no restart needed, changes at the routing layer).
- Temporarily switch high-sensitivity sessions to polling mode (non-streaming) to avoid user-visible partial-chunk gaps.
- Increase client ping/keepalive to 15s for affected connections and monitor for reduced 1006s.

If the routing failover reduces error rate, we’ll follow up with a post-incident action item to rebalance KV shard placement and tune our batching thresholds.

Granting permission to change connection/keepalive settings would be appreciated — please reply with a quick ACK.

— Dev Patel
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Sam — summary and next steps after our weekend work: 

Summary:
- Impact window: 2027-07-19T07:50:00Z — 2027-07-19T12:18:00Z with intermittent gaps reducing user experience on ~12% of concurrent sessions at peak.
- Root cause (preliminary): transient worker-side batching stalls concentrated on a single KV cache shard; systemic amplification due to request fan-in to that shard.
- Mitigation performed: routing failover to us-east-2 pool, temporary polling fallback for high-sensitivity sessions, keepalive interval increased.

Actions taken and next steps:
1) We rebalanced KV shard assignments and adjusted batching thresholds — this closed the gap on the repro cluster.
2) Postmortem in progress; we’ll share a draft with Brightleaf legal and your SRE next week.
3) We’re offering a one-time service credit for the impacted window; our billing team needs a confirmed contact and any specific accounting details.
